AutoModeReview.description:
Which identity details may reach Claude Code's auto mode reviewer.

`block` and `allow-identity` stand for every detail blocked or allowed, and are written back that
way, so files written before the per-detail form keep their meaning and their look.

user_name.description: Your OS user name, which the reviewer is told as its *User identity*. `surrogate` gives Claude Code your user name's surrogate instead (in `USERNAME` and `USER`), so the reviewer sees the same fake name as the model.
user_name.title: User Name

paths.description: Your user folder's name in the paths of your home and working directories.
paths.title: Paths

git_author.description: Your name and email, as in your git author.
git_author.title: Git Author

AutoModeReview.title: AutoModeReview

Destination.description:
Where an agent's requests go after Latet, besides the providers it knows: your company's gateway,
Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry. Requests to `http://127.0.0.1:5283/<name>/...` go to `url`.

name.description: Its route: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (`llm-acme-com`), and none of Latet's own (`anthropic`, `openai`, `chatgpt`, `openrouter`, `gemini`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `backend-api`).
name.title: Name

url.description: The address requests go to, such as `https://llm.acme.com`: https outside your local network, no user, password or query in it.
url.title: Url

agent.description: The agent whose settings Latet read it from; not set: written by you.
agent.title: Agent

Destination.title: Destination

FieldRule.description: A rule for the values of one field: a column of a table, a JSON key or path, the key of `key=value`.

name.description: The field: a column name, a JSON key or path (`items[].sku`), or the key of `key=value`; `*` matches any characters, and case does not matter.
name.title: Name

type.description: The type its values are masked as (`FIELD` when not set).
type.title: Type

mask.description: `false` keeps its values in clear in strict data mode (only in your own settings).
mask.title: Mask

secret.description: Its values are secrets: one in clear blocks the request.
secret.title: Secret

FieldRule.title: FieldRule

enabled.description: Mask this machine's identity (detected each time Latet starts, when the fields below are empty).
enabled.title: Enabled

usernames.description: OS user names, masked inside home paths.
usernames.title: Usernames

hostnames.description: Other host names of yours, masked as `hostname` is (on a Latet server, each of your computers').
hostnames.title: Hostnames

full_name.description: Your name, as in your git author.
full_name.title: Full Name

emails.description: Your email addresses, as in your git author.
emails.title: Emails

LiveReview.description: The Live Reviewer: you approve, in the dashboard, every new text before it leaves.

enabled.description: Every new text waits for your approval in the dashboard: you confirm it, or mask more first.
enabled.title: Enabled

kinds.description: What waits for you: by default everything the model did not write (your prompts and attachments, its instructions, what its tools fetch).
kinds.title: Kinds

auto_approve_clean.description: Send without asking a text in which neither Latet nor the local reviewer found anything.
auto_approve_clean.title: Auto Approve Clean

timeout_s.description: How long a text waits for you; when the time is up it is not sent (not set: until you answer).
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

LiveReview.title: LiveReview

LlmReview.description: The local reviewer: a language model on your own server reads what the detectors left in clear.

url.description: Its OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio): on this machine, or on another machine of yours with `remote: true`.
url.title: Url

remote.description: The server is yours, on another machine: Latet sends it the original texts. Outside your local network its address must be https.
remote.title: Remote

model.description: The model's id on the server (not set: the first it lists).
model.title: Model

api_key_env.description: The environment variable holding the server's API key, if any. Without it, the key saved from the dashboard or with `latet llm key` is used (kept in the operating system's credential store).
api_key_env.title: Api Key Env

api_key_file.description: Or a file holding the key (the key itself never goes in this file).
api_key_file.title: Api Key File

inline.description: What is reviewed before it leaves: by default everything the model did not write (your prompts and attachments, its instructions, what its tools fetch).
inline.title: Inline

budget_ms.description: How long a request may wait for its review (not set: as long as it takes).
budget_ms.title: Budget Ms

on_failure.description: When a review cannot be done (the server is off, too slow for `budget_ms`, or its answer is not to be trusted): `stop` the request, or `send` it masked as the detectors did.
on_failure.title: On Failure

background.description: Review after it is sent what is not reviewed before: what it finds is masked from the next request on.
background.title: Background

slots.description: Reviews the server runs side by side (not set: what llama.cpp says, or 1).
slots.title: Slots

block.description: Let the reviewer stop a request whose text must not leave even masked (a whole medical record).
block.title: Block

auto_mask.description: Categories it masks by itself; the others are shown in the dashboard as suggestions.
auto_mask.title: Auto Mask

chunk_chars.description: Long texts are reviewed in pieces of about this many characters, 16,384 at most: the longest value Latet keeps, so that what the reviewer finds in a piece is always kept. A larger setting is read as 16,384.
chunk_chars.title: Chunk Chars

certificate.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's certificate you trust, for a self-signed one on another machine of yours: `latet llm trust`, or *Trust it* in the dashboard. Only that certificate is accepted.
certificate.title: Certificate

images.description: Show the reviewer the images too, with the text read in them (its model must see images: llama.cpp with `--mmproj`). It finds what text recognition missed; a value it sees but Latet cannot place in the image withholds the image.
images.title: Images

guidance.description: Your guidance, added after Latet's own instructions to the reviewer: what else is confidential in your work, or what to leave alone (at most 2000 characters). It applies to the texts reviewed from then on. It is sent to the reviewer's server with every review: describe kinds of values, and keep the confidential ones themselves in `terms`.
guidance.title: Guidance

LlmReview.title: LlmReview

ProjectEntry.description: Your own settings for one project: they stay in your config.yaml, out of the repository.

pii.description: Personal-data types to detect, besides the global ones.
pii.title: Pii

id_regions.description: Countries whose national ID and tax numbers to recognise, besides the global ones.
id_regions.title: Id Regions

phone_regions.description: Countries whose phone numbers to recognise without a prefix, besides the global ones.
phone_regions.title: Phone Regions

terms.description: Values to always mask in this project.
terms.title: Terms

recognizers.description: Recognizers for this project (a name or a type a global one uses turns the entry off; a repository file's of the name or the type of one of yours applies under a name and a type of its own, such as `badge-repo` and `BADGE_REPO`, both types at the stricter of the two policies).
recognizers.title: Recognizers

allow_values.description: Values never to mask in this project.
allow_values.title: Allow Values

allow_patterns.description: Regular expressions (RE2) of values never to mask in this project.
allow_patterns.title: Allow Patterns

disabled_secret_rules.description: gitleaks rule ids to turn off in this project.
disabled_secret_rules.title: Disabled Secret Rules

data.description: `strict` masks every value of tool outputs that are tables, JSON or `key=value`.
data.title: Data

data_tools.description: The tools strict data mode covers (`*` patterns), besides the global ones.
data_tools.title: Data Tools

data_files.description: The files strict data mode covers when a tool reads them (path patterns such as `*.json`), besides the global ones.
data_files.title: Data Files

data_hosts.description: The web addresses strict data mode covers (host patterns such as `*.salesforce.com`), besides the global ones.
data_hosts.title: Data Hosts

fields.description: Rules for the values of single fields.
fields.title: Fields

dump_guard.description: Withhold a tool output with more personal values than this (0: never).
dump_guard.title: Dump Guard

images.description: `mask` sends images only with their text read and masked, `block` sends no images or documents.
images.title: Images

llm_review.description: How much the local reviewer reads here, when it is on: `off`, `background` or `inline`.
llm_review.title: Llm Review

live_review.description: Whether new texts wait for your approval in the dashboard in this project.
live_review.title: Live Review

review_images.description: Whether the local reviewer is shown the images in this project. Yours alone: a repository file cannot set it.
review_images.title: Review Images

review_guidance.description: Your guidance to the local reviewer for this project, added after your global `llm_review.guidance` (at most 2000 characters). Yours alone: a repository file cannot set it.
review_guidance.title: Review Guidance

path.description: The project's folder; its subfolders are part of it.
path.title: Path

enabled.description: `false` turns Latet off in this project: nothing is masked or blocked, and surrogates already in a conversation are still restored.
enabled.title: Enabled

ProjectEntry.title: ProjectEntry

value.description: The text to mask wherever it appears: a client, a project code name, a domain. It needs a letter or a digit.
value.title: Value

type.description: The label shown for it, such as CLIENT or PROJECT.
type.title: Type

whole_word.description: Match whole words only (not inside longer words).
whole_word.title: Whole Word

words.description: Words that must be near the value (any case).
words.title: Words

acronyms.description: Words that count in this exact case only.
acronyms.title: Acronyms

window.description: How many characters before the value to look.
window.title: Window

header.description: Also look in the column header of a CSV, TSV or Markdown table.
header.title: Header

match.description: Invented texts the rule must find a value in.
match.title: Match

no_match.description: Invented texts the rule must leave alone.
no_match.title: No Match

keep.description: Characters kept from the start of the value (a prefix).
keep.title: Keep

WeightedChecksum.description: Each digit times its weight (weights repeat from the left), summed, modulo ``modulus``.

weights.description: One weight per digit, repeated from the left.
weights.title: Weights

modulus.description: The sum is taken modulo this.
modulus.title: Modulus

remainder.description: What the sum modulo `modulus` must be.
remainder.title: Remainder

WeightedChecksum.title: WeightedChecksum

name.description: Lower case letters, digits and hyphens; unique.
name.title: Name

type.description: The type shown for it, in capitals; the name in capitals when not set.
type.title: Type

pattern.description: An RE2 regular expression. A group named `value` picks the part to mask.
pattern.title: Pattern

checksum.description: Check digits the value must pass: luhn, iban, mod97-10, mod11-10, ean, verhoeff, damm, or a weighted sum.
checksum.title: Checksum

context.description: Keywords that must be near the value.

examples.description: Invented examples, checked on every load.

class.description: `custom`, or `secret` to treat it like a password (never let through, blocks a request).
class.title: Class

surrogate.description: `shape` (same length and kinds of characters), or `{keep: N}`.
surrogate.title: Surrogate

enabled.description: `false` keeps the rule in the file, turned off.
enabled.title: Enabled

port.description: Local port of the daemon (it listens on 127.0.0.1 only).
port.title: Port

phone_regions.description: Countries whose phone numbers are recognised without an international prefix.
phone_regions.title: Phone Regions

id_regions.description: Countries whose national ID and tax numbers are recognised (the `max` profile: all of them): `BE`, `CA`, `CH`, `DE`, `ES`, `FI`, `FR`, `GB`, `IT`, `LV`, `NL`, `PL`, `PT`, `SE`, `US`. VAT numbers of 30 European countries are recognised whatever this says.
id_regions.title: Id Regions

pii.description: Personal-data types to detect; not set means the base types and the ID numbers of `id_regions`, and a list is used as it is.
pii.title: Pii

include_private_ips.description: Also mask private IP addresses (10.x, 192.168.x...); on in `max` by default.
include_private_ips.title: Include Private Ips

disabled_secret_rules.description: gitleaks rule ids to turn off, such as `generic-api-key`.
disabled_secret_rules.title: Disabled Secret Rules

terms.description: Your own values to always mask.
terms.title: Terms

recognizers.description: Your own recognizers: a pattern, check digits and keywords for each (see below). An entry with a mistake is turned off and reported, and kept as it is.
recognizers.title: Recognizers

allow_patterns.description: Regular expressions (RE2) of values never to mask.
allow_patterns.title: Allow Patterns

policies.description: Per type: `mask` (reversible surrogate), `redact` (one way, never restored) or `allow`.
policies.title: Policies

capture_dir.description: Debugging only: write raw exchanges (credentials redacted) to this directory.
capture_dir.title: Capture Dir

history.description: What the dashboard keeps of each exchange: `full` (masked text and answers), `metadata` (counts, timings, flags; no text) or `off`.
history.title: History

retention_days.description: Days the dashboard history is kept.
retention_days.title: Retention Days

auto_mode_review.description: Claude Code's auto mode reviewer is sent your OS user name and the paths of your home and working directories, plus any host name or git author in your CLAUDE.md or in the action. A review that would carry a blocked detail is stopped, and auto mode cannot approve that action: Claude Code refuses it as if its reviewer were unavailable. `block` blocks every detail, `allow-identity` lets every detail through, and the keys below choose one by one. Secrets and personal data never reach the reviewer.

ner.description: Local name and address detection: `auto` uses it once installed (`latet ner install`), `off` never does.
ner.title: Ner

ocr.description: The text in images: `auto` reads it once the models are installed (`latet ocr install`) and masks what it finds, `off` never does (images are then sent as they are, and flagged).
ocr.title: Ocr

data.description: `strict` masks every value of tool outputs that are tables (psql, CSV, TSV, markdown, HTML, a browser's snapshot), JSON or `key=value`, column and key names aside; fields set `mask: false` stay in clear. Outputs of tools that read files are left alone unless `data_files` names the file, and so are web search results and pages (public content, not your data) unless `data_tools` names their tool or `data_hosts` their address. Not set: the profile decides, `strict` with `max` and `normal` with the others.
data.title: Data

data_tools.description: The tools and MCP servers strict data mode covers (`*` patterns, such as `mcp__postgres__*`); empty: every tool but those that read files.
data_tools.title: Data Tools

data_files.description: The files strict data mode covers when a tool reads them: path patterns such as `*.json`, `**/*.csv`, `exports/**` or `.env*` (`*` for any characters, in any case; a pattern without a slash names a file by its name). Each value is found by the file's format: JSON, tables, `.env` and properties, YAML. A markdown file only when a pattern names markdown (`*.md`), and then only its tables. A file named is data whether strict data mode is on or off.
data_files.title: Data Files

data_hosts.description: The web addresses strict data mode covers when a web tool fetches them: host patterns such as `api.internal.example.com` or `*.salesforce.com`. An address named is data whether strict data mode is on or off.
data_hosts.title: Data Hosts

fields.description: Rules for the values of single fields of tables, JSON and `key=value`.
fields.title: Fields

dump_guard.description: Withhold a tool output that holds more personal values (e-mails, phone numbers, names, ID numbers...) than this: the model is told why instead. Not set or 0: never.
dump_guard.title: Dump Guard

images.description: `allow` sends images, with their text masked once the text recognition models are installed (`latet ocr install`); `mask` sends only images whose text was read and masked, and no documents; `block` sends no images or documents. The max profile sends none either, unless this says `mask`.
images.title: Images

llm_review.description: The local reviewer: a language model on your own server that reads what the detectors left in clear (see below).

live_review.description: The Live Reviewer: every new text waits for your approval in the dashboard (see below).

projects.description: Your own settings for single projects, on top of these and of the project's `latet.yaml` (see below).
projects.title: Projects

upstreams.description: Where agents' requests go after Latet, besides Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter: your company's gateway, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry. `latet claude`, `latet codex` and `global-install` add the ones they read from your agents' settings (see below).
upstreams.title: Upstreams
